key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, travel speed, and welding current affect molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability in distinct ways.
engineering_relevance: These trends can guide welding-parameter selection for Invar components used in aerospace composite molds.
method: Parameter studies spanning 5–6 kW, 0.5–0.8 m/min, and 150–170 A
evidence_signal: Within the tested ranges, higher laser power increased penetration and promoted arc deflection, higher speed reduced penetration and width while promoting arc deformation, and higher current widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract reports parameter trends but no quantitative validation errors or weld-defect outcomes, limiting confidence in extrapolation beyond the tested ranges.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
